evidence:
SOURCE STRUCTURE SUPPORTS A GRADED REWARD. tests/scoring.toml:1-11 gives gates render=0.0/constraints=0.0, weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05; tests/tools/score.py:41-48 computes a weighted mean of three continuous dimension scores and zeros only on gate failure or functional<=0.05; test.sh:213-227 runs gates then scored. Parsed with tomllib: functional = 44 binary criteria, weighted_mean, total weight 61.0 (weights 1/1.5/2); polish = 5 binary, weighted_mean, total 9.5; visual = 5 Likert(5) weight 1 each, weighted_mean; each gate = 1 binary all_pass criterion. So the scored reward can take many intermediate values. Gates are simple per Colderwater lesson 4: render (wrong password refused, correct sign-in shows a workspace) and constraints (add one candidate, reload, Observer reads it in an independent context) - these exclude dead/static apps without pulling scored difficulty into the gate. Functional weight is spread across independent areas: S intake 3, M moves 7, L interview places 5.5, R roles 7.5, C stale 2, B multi-card/undo 10, A activity 2, N notes 1, V live board 2, T conversations 9.5, U unread/seen 5.5, K candidates 4.5, D restart 1.5 (sum 61). functional/prompt.md:13 tells the judge 'score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures', 'A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row', and to re-set up a broken setup on a new job so other rows stay observable; line 61 preserves completed observations on tool failure. Floor 0.05 means a gate-passing shell must earn >3.05/61 functional weight before polish/visual count, which stops a dead app farming craft, as intended. Thought experiments: a fake app that passes both gates but implements nothing else plausibly earns at most hro_add_candidate (1) and part of nothing else, i.e. functional ~0.016 < floor -> reward 0 (correct). A board-only app (moves, order, reject/reopen, places, roles, notes, restart, but no multi-select/undo, no live updates, weak conversations) would pass roughly S+M(minus undo legs)+L(minus hro_undo_full)+part of R+N+D, i.e. on the order of 15-25/61 functional, plus Likert visual credit -> an intermediate reward; a full app approaches 1. So the design discriminates on paper. 

COUPLING THAT REDUCES (BUT DOES NOT COLLAPSE) DISCRIMINATION (P2, overlaps row 28): several permission rows require same-kind positive controls for unrelated features. functional/judge.toml:175 hro_observer_readonly needs Rafael's successful move, multi-card move, reject, undo, add, open-job and note requests as controls; :184 hro_candidate_no_staff 'Fails if ... the staff control did not succeed' over the same list; :193 hro_anonymous needs 'A signed-in success of each' incl. multi-card move, undo and message. An app with perfect server authorization but no multi-card move or no undo therefore also loses these 3.5 weight units, on top of B (10) and the undo legs of reject_reason/reopen/undo_full. Similarly, live-update absence zeroes polish hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread (polish/judge.toml:25 and :34 'preservation cannot be shown and this row is 0') = 4/9.5 polish, in addition to functional live rows (hro_live_board 2, hro_unread_counts 2, hro_unread_scrolled_up 2, hro_seen 1.5, part of hro_msg_exchange). These correlated losses are bounded (~0.1-0.17 of total reward each) and are features the brief explicitly asks for (instruction.md:3,5,7), so they do not make the reward all-or-nothing; they compress the middle of the band. 

UNMEASURED COLLAPSE MODE (risk): functional is one batched claude-code session (functional/judge.toml:3-4, mode=batched, timeout=9000) over 14 long protocols (Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D) with many independent contexts, replays and timed observations. If that session crashes or exhausts its budget before returning criteria (Colderwater lesson 11: infra crashes zero a dimension), functional=0, the 0.05 floor fails and reward is 0 for any app, including a correct one - an all-or-nothing outcome unrelated to quality. Whether partial batched results survive a timeout is not established by anything I read. 

MISSING REQUIRED EVIDENCE: raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The only runtime evidence is a scripted golden driver (via-solve.log: 26 groups PASS, hashes verified), which is not a configured judge run and gives no reward for any weak or partial app. REVIEW_POLICY.md requires a separate hash-bound reward-discrimination record before local clearance. No measured spread across partial-quality apps exists for this candidate, so per the skill I do not upgrade the on-paper analysis to Pass.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that could score 0: a correct app whose functional judge session (batched, 9000 s, 14 protocols) is cut off or crashes before emitting criteria gets functional=0, fails the 0.05 floor and receives reward 0 despite passing gates and earning polish/visual - not measured either way. Partial app compressed: an app with correct server authorization but no multi-card move/undo loses hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff and hro_anonymous (3.5/61) for missing controls in addition to the B rows (10/61).
suggested_fix: Produce the policy-required reward-discrimination record: run the full configured verifier on the golden plus at least two mutated partial apps (e.g. no undo/multi-select; no live updates) and record the per-dimension rewards and judge durations; optionally scope the permission rows' controls to request kinds the app actually offers so missing features are not deducted again there.
